title: Pure-section normalization of the quotient tensor augmentation
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X a scheme. Let chain be a natural transformation from the completed-coefficient total tensor to the specified finite-tensor Roos complex [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]. Suppose that on each pair (P,Q) its component is tensorOperationUnit, the quotient Roos unit on the total tensor followed by the Roos image of the normalized tensorTowerIso [lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models]. Then chain satisfies IsTensorChain: at every positive quotient n and every homogeneous pure tensor x tensor y its first coordinate is the tensor of the two quotient-unit sections, and its shifted Roos coordinate is zero. No compactness, constructibility or invertibility hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Integral reconstruction through thm-sf-pf-adic: strict quotient-tensor augmentation; Bhatt--Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 6.5.5, Stacks 03EL, 07A4, 0941.

proof.text: Substitute the stated component identity for chain. Apply tensorOperationUnit_coordinates. Its second assertion immediately gives the zero shifted coordinate. Its first assertion expresses the first coordinate as the product quotient augmentation followed by the product of the strict tensor-tower comparison maps.

Compose this first identity with the product projection to level n and evaluate the degree p+q map on the homogeneous pure tensor. Naturality of product maps reduces its right side to the level n strict tensor map applied to the level n augmentation.

The uniquely normalized augmentation augmentation_existsUnique sends this tensor to the quotient generator with scalar 1. The normalization supplied by tensorTowerModel sends that generator to the tensor of the two quotient-unit sections. Compose these equalities to obtain the first clause of IsTensorChain. These formulas include zero sections and the empty scheme.
